notes: This document changes shape halfway through. Its general provisions are numbered 1.1 and 3.2.1; the 43 zone chapters that follow are headed by the zone itself and number their provisions (1), (2), (3). Only the first form was once recognised, and only its two-part variant, so the entire second half - every lot area and setback in the bylaw - sat inside one clause titled CONFLICTING PROVISIONS at 98,111 characters.

Most questions here therefore ask for a zone standard, which is exactly the text that was unreachable. They cite as MHP(1) and R1(3): '(1) PERMITTED USES' appears under all 43 zones, so the zone code is carried into the citation or one number names 43 different provisions.
Definitions were inheriting section 1.5, because the heading that introduces them reads 'SECTION 2- DEFINITIONS' and nothing matched it.

questions.question: What is the minimum lot area for a single detached dwelling in the R1 zone?
questions.why: A zone standard, which is the text that was unreachable. The number must come from the R1 chapter and no other.

questions.question: How much frontage does a single detached lot need in R1?
questions.why: Pairs with the lot area: both values sit in one table, and a shift would take them from a neighbouring zone.

questions.question: What can I build in a mini home park zone?
questions.why: The permitted-use list of a zone chapter, cited with its zone code.

questions.question: What is a backyard suite?
questions.why: Definitions cite section 2, where the bylaw puts them, not the 1.5 they were inheriting.

questions.question: Can I put a granny flat on my property for a caretaker?
questions.why: The regulations never say 'granny flat'. Only semantic retrieval bridges this.
